claims.title: Amerindian settlement of the Guianas
claims.summary: Arawak, Carib and Warrau peoples settle the rivers, coast and highlands of present-day Guyana, developing cassava farming, fishing and riverine trade.

sources.label: Guyana and Belize: Country Studies
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: The Wild Coast and El Dorado
claims.summary: Spanish and other navigators probe the rivers of the 'Wild Coast' in search of the golden kingdom of El Dorado, but find no empire to conquer.

claims.title: Founding of Essequibo
claims.summary: The Dutch establish the colony of Essequibo, the oldest of the three, followed by Berbice (1627) and Demerara (split from Essequibo in 1745).

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Guyana
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: The engineered sugar coast
claims.summary: Dutch planters drain the coastal plain with polders, dams, canals and koker sluice-gates, building a below-sea-level sugar landscape worked by enslaved Africans.

sources.label: Guyana and Belize: Country Studies
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: The Berbice slave rebellion
claims.summary: Enslaved Africans led by Cuffy rise in Berbice, holding much of the colony for almost a year in one of the largest slave revolts in the Americas before being suppressed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guyana: From the Amerindian peoples of the Guiana highlands and three Dutch plantation colonies to British Guiana, a society forged by slavery and indenture, and an independent nation now transformed by offshore oil.", terralore.co/country/GUY/chronicle#ev-1763-the-berbice-slave-rebellion, claim TL:GUY:event:1763:the-berbice-slave-rebellion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Stabroek (Georgetown)
claims.summary: A British occupying force lays out the town of Stabroek at the mouth of the Demerara River; renamed Georgetown in 1812, it becomes the colony's capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guyana: From the Amerindian peoples of the Guiana highlands and three Dutch plantation colonies to British Guiana, a society forged by slavery and indenture, and an independent nation now transformed by offshore oil.", terralore.co/country/GUY/chronicle#ev-1781-founding-of-stabroek-georgetown, claim TL:GUY:event:1781:founding-of-stabroek-georgetown, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Demerara rising
claims.summary: Thousands of enslaved people in Demerara rebel, believing emancipation has been withheld; the revolt is brutally suppressed, and the death of missionary John Smith galvanises British abolitionists.

sources.label: Guyana and Belize: Country Studies

claims.title: Creation of British Guiana
claims.summary: Britain unites the colonies of Essequibo, Demerara and Berbice into a single Crown colony, British Guiana, with Georgetown as its capital.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Guyana
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Emancipation and Indian indenture
claims.summary: Full emancipation takes effect on 1 August 1838; the first indentured labourers from India arrive on 5 May 1838, beginning decades of immigration that reshape the colony's population.

sources.label: Guyana and Belize: Country Studies
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: End of Indian indenture
claims.summary: Indentured immigration from India is brought to a close after some 250,000 people have come to British Guiana, leaving Indo-Guyanese the colony's largest ethnic group.

sources.label: Guyana and Belize: Country Studies
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: PPP victory and suspended constitution
claims.summary: The People's Progressive Party wins the first elections under universal suffrage and Jagan becomes chief minister, but Britain suspends the constitution and sends troops after 133 days.

sources.label: Guyana and Belize: Country Studies
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: The PPP splits along ethnic lines
claims.summary: Forbes Burnham breaks with Jagan and forms the People's National Congress; the two parties harden into Afro- and Indo-Guyanese blocs that dominate national politics.

claims.title: Independence of Guyana
claims.summary: British Guiana becomes the independent nation of Guyana within the Commonwealth, with Forbes Burnham as first prime minister and Cheddi Jagan as opposition leader.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Guyana
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: The Cooperative Republic
claims.summary: Guyana is proclaimed a cooperative republic, marking the date of Cuffy's 1763 rebellion as Republic Day while remaining within the Commonwealth.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Guyana
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Nationalisation of the economy
claims.summary: Burnham's government nationalises the foreign-owned bauxite and sugar industries, bringing most of the economy under state control in a 'cooperative socialist' programme.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guyana: From the Amerindian peoples of the Guiana highlands and three Dutch plantation colonies to British Guiana, a society forged by slavery and indenture, and an independent nation now transformed by offshore oil.", terralore.co/country/GUY/chronicle#ev-1971-nationalisation-of-the-economy, claim TL:GUY:event:1971:nationalisation-of-the-economy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Jonestown tragedy
claims.summary: At the Peoples Temple settlement of Jonestown, more than 900 followers of the American preacher Jim Jones die in a mass murder-suicide after the killing of a visiting U.S. congressman.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guyana: From the Amerindian peoples of the Guiana highlands and three Dutch plantation colonies to British Guiana, a society forged by slavery and indenture, and an independent nation now transformed by offshore oil.", terralore.co/country/GUY/chronicle#ev-1978-the-jonestown-tragedy, claim TL:GUY:event:1978:the-jonestown-tragedy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Burnham; Hoyte succeeds
claims.summary: Forbes Burnham dies in office and is succeeded by Desmond Hoyte, who begins to liberalise the economy and ease political controls.

claims.title: Return of Jagan and free elections
claims.summary: Internationally observed elections return Cheddi Jagan and the PPP to power after 28 years, restoring multiparty democracy; his widow Janet Jagan later becomes Guyana's first woman president.

claims.title: First offshore oil discovery
claims.summary: ExxonMobil and partners make the first major oil discovery in the offshore Stabroek block, beginning Guyana's transformation into a significant petroleum producer.

claims.title: Guyana takes Essequibo case to the ICJ
claims.summary: Guyana files proceedings at the International Court of Justice seeking to confirm the 1899 arbitral award fixing its boundary with Venezuela.

claims.title: First oil production
claims.summary: Production begins in the Stabroek block; within a few years Guyana exceeds 600,000 barrels a day and becomes one of the world's fastest-growing economies.
